name: Érainn
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Érainn hold a place in the record of Ireland. In the last centuries before the common era, a Celtic people reached the southwest of Ireland. The geographer Ptolemy called them the Iverni. Scholars call this people the Érainn. They were not the first settlers of the island. Those who built the Megalithic Civilization came first, and their names are unknown.  They were not the last migrants either. The Lagin and Féni peoples came after them. Some scholars trace the Fomorians and the Fir Bolg to these early people.
